description: This topic covers the evolution of computers from early mechanical calculating devices to modern artificial intelligence-based machines. It is highly crucial for the Computer Knowledge section of competitive exams.

sections.title: Early Calculating Devices
sections.description: Major mechanical devices used for calculations before the development of modern electronic computers.

key_concepts.explanation: Considered the world's first calculating device. It was invented in ancient China primarily for basic addition and subtraction.
Developed by Blaise Pascal in 1642, it was the first mechanical calculator that worked on a system of gears and wheels.
Designed by Charles Babbage in 1837, it was the first general-purpose computer concept featuring fundamental elements like input, output, and memory.

key_associations.extra_info: He is credited with inventing the Difference Engine and conceptually designing the Analytical Engine.
She wrote the first algorithm intended to be processed by Babbage's Analytical Engine.

sections.title: First and Second Generation of Computers
sections.description: The early electronic era of computers and their core underlying hardware technologies.

historical_events.significance: Utilized Vacuum Tubes as core components. They were enormous in size, generated immense heat, consumed high electricity, and relied solely on Machine Language (0s and 1s).
Replaced Vacuum Tubes with Transistors. This made computers relatively smaller, faster, more energy-efficient, and introduced Assembly Language.

key_associations.extra_info: Built by J. Presper Eckert and John Mauchly, it is the most famous example of a First Generation computer.
Co-invented the transistor in 1947 along with John Bardeen and Walter Brattain at Bell Labs.

sections.title: Third and Fourth Generation of Computers
sections.description: The rise of microelectronics and the dawn of personal desktop computers.

historical_events.significance: Marked by the use of Integrated Circuits (ICs). This era introduced operating systems, keyboards, and monitors, replacing punch cards.
Powered by Microprocessors and VLSI (Very Large Scale Integration) technology. This generation saw the rise of the Internet, GUIs (Graphical User Interfaces), and Personal Computers (PCs).

key_concepts.explanation: A small silicon chip containing thousands of transistors and other electronic components. It was invented by Jack Kilby.
A single silicon chip that contains the entire Central Processing Unit (CPU). The Intel 4004 was the world's first commercially available microprocessor.

sections.title: Fifth Generation of Computers
sections.description: Present and future technologies enabling machines to possess human-like cognitive abilities.

historical_events.significance: Relies heavily on Parallel Processing, Machine Learning, and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to create intelligent systems.

key_concepts.explanation: The technology that enables machines to simulate human intelligence, including learning, reasoning, and decision-making capabilities.
The technology of embedding millions of transistors on a single silicon microchip, forming the hardware basis for fifth-generation computing.
An advanced computing paradigm utilizing the principles of quantum mechanics to process data at unprecedented speeds, using 'Qubits' instead of traditional binary bits.

sections.title: Important Facts and Milestones
sections.description: Crucial one-liner facts related to the history of computers in India and the world.

key_associations.extra_info: He conceptualized the Turing Machine and played a pivotal role in breaking the German Enigma code during World War II.
He invented the first computer mouse in the 1960s, which was originally made of wood.

important_facts.fact: Siddharth was the first personal computer built in India, manufactured by the Electronic Corporation of India.
PARAM 8000 was India's first supercomputer, successfully developed in 1991 by C-DAC, Pune.
Cray-1, designed by Seymour Cray in 1976, is widely recognized as the world's first successful supercomputer.
